found.summary:
Self-hosting MiniMax H3 in ComfyUI is practical on a single GPU. Native support came in ComfyUI v0.30.0 (PR #15224, merged 2026-08-03). The current version is v0.42.1. The official I2V template loads four files: the pruned INT8 ConvRot FL2VA DiT (20.97 GB), the Qwen3-VL-32B NVFP4-AWQ text encoder (15.69 GB), the INT8 video VAE (2.81 GB) and the fp32 audio VAE (0.61 GB). Its defaults are res_multistep + simple, 20 steps, and shift 12 / audio shift 3. MiniMax and SGLang examples use 50 steps. Your 30 steps is not an official default. Comfy-Org has no NVFP4 DiT; community NVFP4 DiTs (12.5 GB) only help on Blackwell. In ComfyUI's code, NVFP4 and MXFP8 run natively only on compute capability 10 or higher (B200, RTX 5090, RTX PRO 6000). On H100, L40S, 4090 and A100 the weights stay 4-bit and are dequantized for each matmul. That is fine for the text encoder, but a reason to use INT8 ConvRot for the DiT, which needs PyTorch cu130.

Your Civitai clips almost certainly came from the stock base weights, not an NSFW finetune. Civitai model 2821932 / version 3216500 is CivitaiOfficial's 'MiniMax H3 – Comfy' page. Its primary file is the full 66.28 GB bf16 DiT. ComfyUI has an open, still unfixed bug where full (unpruned) checkpoints flicker in brightness every 17 frames, while pruned ones are clean. That matters for loops.

Workload: 768x1024 at 10 s (243 frames) is 55,296 video tokens, about 1.5x the standard 1344x768 5 s benchmark (37,296). The game frame 896x1152 costs exactly the same as that benchmark. Measured points:
- 4090D, 1344x768, 107 frames: 13.7 s per step (INT8)
- 5090: 5.2 s per step at 864x480
- 3090 Ti, about 1 MP for 10 s: 52–55 s per step
- 5070 Ti 16 GB, 1280x736, 15 s: about 80 s per step
- 4×H200 (SGLang), 1344x768, 5 s, 50 steps: 74–84 s

My extrapolation for 768x1024 at 10 s and 20 steps: about 3–5 min on an H100 or H200, 7–12 min on a 5090 or PRO 6000, and about 11 min on a 4090 or A100.

Memory: VRAM is not the limit, because dynamic VRAM streams weights and 16 GB cards finish 1 MP / 15 s clips. System RAM is the limit: plan at least 64 GB for the INT8 stack and 96–128 GB for bf16, or use --fast-disk.

License: no clause bans adult content. But the community license excludes the US, EU, UK and South Korea for use, distribution and display of outputs. That is the real blocker for a game sold worldwide.

Loops: I found no official guidance. One Civitai workflow says giving the same image as first and last frame loops cleanly.

facts.fact: Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3 diffusion_models (identical sizes for fl2va and ref2va): bf16 66.28 GB; int8_convrot 34.04 GB; pruned_bf16 40.23 GB; pruned_fp8_scaled 20.96 GB; pruned_int8_convrot 20.97 GB; pruned_w6a8 15.98 GB. The repo has no NVFP4 or MXFP8 diffusion model. Repo last modified 2026-09-29.

Comfy-Org text encoders: qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_bf16 51.51 GB, _int8_convrot 27.14 GB, _nvfp4_awq 15.69 GB. The NVFP4 file is converted from cybermotaz/Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct-NVFP4. README: 'This nvfp4 text encoder does not require Blackwell GPU to use.' VAEs: video fp16 5.21 GB, video int8_convrot 2.81 GB, audio fp32 0.61 GB. Turbo LoRAs 1.96 GB each. Fun ControlNet patches 2.30–8.38 GB.

Comfy-Org README: 'For diffusion models prefer int8_convrot if you are able to use pytorch with cu130. fp8_scaled should only be used if you cannot use int8_convrot.' kijai on ComfyUI #15419: 'Update to cu130 minimum to use the int8 models.'

MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 (created 2026-07-28, not gated, license date 2026-08-02) holds BF16, CFG-distilled checkpoints in both diffusers and original layouts. The repo totals about 498 GB. Per variant: transformer about 66.3 GB (13 shards), Qwen3-VL-32B text encoder about 66.7 GB (14 shards), video VAE source 10.4 GB, audio VAE 0.605 GB. Transformer: 50 layers, hidden 5376, 56 heads, FFN 14336. Scheduler shift 12.0 (video) / 3.0 (audio).

GGUF derivatives: unsloth/MiniMax-H3-GGUF fl2va_pruned Q2_K 6.72 GB, Q3_K 8.76, Q4_K 11.42, Q5_0 13.92, Q6_K 16.59, Q8_0 21.44 GB, plus text-encoder GGUF Q2_K_M 13.10 GB and Q4_K_M 18.22 GB (updated 2026-10-16). Abiray/MiniMax-H3-Pruned-GGUF: Q3_K_M 8.90 to Q8_0 21.58 GB. Uncensored ('heretic') text encoders: nif0 GGUF Q4_K_M 14.93 GB; coolthor nvfp4 15.68 GB (gated).

NVFP4 and W4A8 DiT derivatives: MATLOWAI/minimax-h3-nvfp4 pruned 12.53 GB; Abiray pruned nvfp4 12.53 GB; rockerBOO pruned nvfp4 20.07 GB and full 34.42 GB; Kijai and AX1Y2JP pruned w4a8_mixed 12.54 GB. The MATLOWAI card says the NVFP4 file is for Blackwell + cu130 only: 'Any other GPU: no. ComfyUI falls back to dequantised matmuls, which is slower than int8_convrot.' It measured 0.84x wall time vs W4A8 at 29k tokens on an RTX PRO 6000.

ComfyUI source: supports_nvfp4_compute() returns False when CUDA compute capability major < 10. supports_mxfp8_compute() also needs major >= 10 and torch >= 2.10. FP8 compute needs sm89+ (Ada) or sm90+. Disabled formats are dequantized to the compute dtype ('emulated ops' in the load log). So NVFP4 is native only on B200 (sm100) and RTX 5090 / RTX PRO 6000 (sm120). It is emulated on H100/H200 (sm90), L40S/4090 (sm89) and A100 (sm80). FP8 is native on L40S/4090/H100 and emulated on A100/3090.

Native MiniMax H3 support is ComfyUI PR #15224 by kijai, merged 2026-08-03 and shipped in v0.30.0 (released 2026-08-03). It added EmptyMiniMaxH3LatentAV, MiniMaxH3ImageToVideo, MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo, MiniMaxH3SigmaShift (shown as 'ModelSamplingMiniMaxH3') and CLIPLoader type 'minimax'. Later additions: MiniMaxH3AddGuide v0.34.0; Fun ControlNet and sparse attention v0.35.0; FastH3 v0.36.0; w6a8 v0.38.0 (2026-09-29). Latest release is v0.42.1 (2026-10-19).

Official templates: video_minimax_h3_i2v, _t2v, _r2v, _i2v_continuation, _multiframe_reference, _fun_controlnet_union, plus FastH3. The I2V template loads minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot, qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq (type minimax), video_vae_int8_convrot and audio_vae_fp32. It uses res_multistep + simple at 20 base steps. An optional lightx2v 8-step turbo LoRA is off by default. Default canvas is 0.4 MP.

Steps and shift per the ComfyUI docs: 20 steps by default (turbo off); 8 with turbo for T2V/I2V. Simple shots: 12–16 steps often enough. High-frequency detail improves up to ~50. Audio needs 12+. Sampler res_multistep + simple; shift 12 / audio_shift 3 from the model definition. MiniMax/SGLang examples use num_inference_steps 50 with flow_shift 12.0 and audio_flow_shift 3.0. So 30 steps is not an official default.

Fewer-step options: lightx2v FL2VA Turbo 8-step and 4-step v1.0 768p LoRAs (1.96 GB ComfyUI files) were trained at 1344x768 with shift 6 / 3; the 544p turbo versions use 12 / 3. FastH3 8-step V2 (FastVideo) pruned int8 is 22.13 GB, with steps fixed at 8 and shift 10/3. DMAD 4-step uses lcm, shift 12 / audio 2. Also: Kijai PDMD 2- and 4-step LoRAs, and alibaba-pai Acc 8-step LoRAs (1.37 GB). Turbo shortens the schedule, not per-step time, and the docs say it softens fine detail.

Canvas rules from nodes_minimax_h3.py: MAX_PIXELS = 768*1344 = 1,032,192; sizes are multiples of 32; frame grid is 17k+5 (124, 141, …, 192, …, 243); latent T = ((frames-5)//17)*5+2. Video tokens: 768x1024 at 124 f = 28,416, at 243 f = 55,296. 864x1152 (3:4, 0.995 MP, under the cap) at 243 f = 69,984. 896x1152 (the game frame) equals the cap exactly and has the same tokens as 1344x768: 37,296 at 124 f.

MiniMaxH3ImageToVideo stretches first_frame to the canvas with no crop, but center-cover-crops last_frame. It anchors them at frame 0 and frame_count-1. An off-aspect image used as both frames therefore yields different pixels at the two ends. MiniMaxH3AddGuide (v0.34.0+) can anchor an image or a 17k+5-frame clip at any frame_idx, including negative values counted from the end.

Your Civitai workflow's UNET 'minimaxh3/civitai/2821932/3216500' is CivitaiOfficial's 'MiniMax H3' base-model page, version 'Comfy MiniMax H3'. Its files hash-match the Comfy-Org repo (fl2va/ref2va int8_convrot, pruned int8, all three text encoders, both VAEs). The version's primary file is a 66.28 GB bf16 Diffusion Model, i.e. the full unpruned DiT. So your clips were very likely made with the unmodified base weights, not an NSFW finetune. The text encoder was nvfp4_awq and the video VAE fp16.

Full (unpruned) H3 checkpoints in ComfyUI show a brightness dip and frame stutter every 17 frames: full INT8 and full BF16 both pulse, pruned INT8 is clean. The cause is traced to model.py casting time_embedder output to the compute dtype ('t_emb = self.time_embedder(t_vals).to(dtype)'). That line is still present on master as of 2026-10-20.

Your FL2VA prompt opens with the I2VA instruction ('For the target video, at 0.00 seconds … <Picture 1> … is fully referenced.') even though last_frame is wired. The official guide's FL2VA line is: 'How the reference pictures align with the target video — Picture 1 (from Shot 1) aligns with the 0.00-second mark of the target video; Picture 2 (from Shot N) aligns with the S.SS-second mark of the target video.'

Speed (consumer GPUs, ComfyUI or SGLang):
- RTX 3090, 864x480, 124 f, 20 steps, pruned int8: 9.0 s/it (6.57 with Sage).
- RTX 3090, 1344x768, 362 f: 188 s/step with comfy-kitchen attention, 420 s/step with PyTorch attention.
- RTX 3090 Ti, '1 MP 10 s': 52–55 s/it.
- RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB, 1280x736, 362 f, 20 steps: ~79–83 s/step, 26–29 min total.
- RTX 5090 (60 GB RAM), 864x480, 124 f, 20 steps, bf16 streamed: 5.2 s/step, 141–146 s per request.
- RTX 4090 D, 1344x768, 107 f, 20 NFE (SGLang): int8+FA 303 s, bf16 406 s.
- RTX PRO 6000, 1920x1088, 15 s, 20 steps: 54 min with Sage vs 1 h 34 min without.

Speed (datacenter GPUs, SGLang):
- 4×H200, 1344x768, 5 s, 50 steps, bf16: 74–84 s end to end (denoise 71.7–79 s), peak 94.3 GB per GPU with Ulysses4.
- 4×H100: TP2+Ulysses2 is the fastest topology, 66 GB peak per GPU.
- 1×B200 (VDN-H3 hybrid attention, not dense), 1344x768, 345 f: 7.45 s/NFE bf16 at 156 GB peak.
- 1×RTX PRO 6000 (VDN-H3): 20.27 s/NFE.
I found no ComfyUI benchmark for a single H100, A100 or L40S. A third-party L40S figure: 960x544 10 s in ~7.2 min, 38.9 GB VRAM peak, 46.7 GB RAM.

My estimate for 768x1024, 243 frames, 20 steps (about 5.7 PFLOP per step), scaled from the measured points: H100/H200 ~10–14 s/step (≈3.5–5 min per clip); B200 ~5–7 s/step (≈2 min); RTX 5090 / PRO 6000 ~20–36 s/step (≈7–12 min); RTX 4090 int8 ~33 s/step (≈11 min); A100 ~30 s/step (≈10 min); L40S ~28–45 s/step (≈9–15 min). Add about 30–60 s for text encode and VAE decode, plus 1–3 min for the first model load. A 5 s clip (124 f) costs roughly 0.35–0.5x as much. 8-step turbo costs about 0.4x of 20 steps.
facts.source: Inference from the benchmark points above (SGLang cookbook, ComfyUI issues #15263, #15665)

facts.fact: VRAM: dynamic VRAM streams weights, so card size mainly sets speed. 16 GB cards finish 1280x736 / 15 s; 24 GB cards run pruned int8 (3090 peaked 19.6–23.7 GB at 1280–1344x704–768, 192 f). Resident fits: 32 GB = pruned int8 DiT; 48 GB = pruned int8 or full int8 (34 GB); 80 GB = pruned bf16 (40 GB); 96 GB = full bf16 (66 GB; peaked ~75 of 96 GB at 1920x1088 15 s without Sage); 141/180 GB = everything, including the 51.5 GB bf16 text encoder. GPU-side peak for the int8+nvfp4 stack at 864x480 / 124 f was ~26–32 GiB.

System RAM: by default ComfyUI keeps a host copy of every model file. A 5070 Ti with the int8 DiT + nvfp4 TE + fp16 VAE stack showed 45.4 GiB RSS, or 12.6 GiB with --fast-disk. A 3090 with 32 GB RAM was OOM-killed at 29.9 GB, and ran in 7.5 GB with --disable-pinned-memory. An RTX 5090 with 60 GB RAM on the unpruned bf16 stack was OOM-killed at load (55.6 GB anonymous memory) and needed --fast-disk. ComfyUI v0.35.0 (PR #15927) respects the container cgroup memory limit.

Version regressions:
- RTX 5090 on ComfyUI v0.41.0, same workflow: PyTorch 2.12.0+cu130 ran ~16.8 s/it; 2.14.1+cu130 ran ~62.9 s/it.
- Around 2026-10-12, users reported 2x-slower H3; --disable-comfy-compiler fixed it for some.
- v0.35.0 crashed some 16 GB cards; --vram-headroom 1 and/or --disable-comfy-compiler stabilized them.

License territory: 'Applicable Territory' means worldwide excluding the 'Excluded Territories': the EU, the UK, the Republic of Korea and the USA. The grant is 'Solely within the Applicable Territory'. Section V.4: 'You may not use, reproduce, modify, distribute, or display the MiniMax H3 Works or any of their Outputs or results outside the Applicable Territory.' AUP item 1 bans 'Use outside the Applicable Territory'. People in those regions must apply: https://platform.minimax.io/h3-license (a JS page; I could not read its fields).

Adult content: neither the license nor the AUP bans sexual content explicitly. Relevant AUP items: #2 (comply with applicable law and third-party rights); #6 (no use that 'exploits or harms … minors'); #12 (no public posting 'without clearly and prominently disclosing that such information and/or content is machine-generated'); #13 (no impersonation without consent); #15 (no use that 'violates or disregards the social, ethical, or moral standards of other countries or regions', which is vague). The README's porn moderation applies only to the hosted H3-Context-IR API, not the local weights.

Commercial use: Section IV.1 requires separate written authorization above US$20M yearly revenue (email api@minimax.io). IV.2: 'You shall prominently display "MiniMax H3" on the user interface of commercial product or service that uses MiniMax H3 or MiniMax H3 Works.' VI.4: 'MiniMax claims no rights over the Outputs you generate.' V.3 bars using outputs to improve other AI models. Comfy's docs say users outside the excluded territories and under $20M are covered with a 'Powered by MiniMax H3' credit, 'the same territory rule applies to where your outputs are used'. Otherwise Comfy, the 'only official reseller', sells licenses from $5,000/month (Professional: up to 10 users, ~46,250 video-seconds included).

Loops: the ComfyUI docs give no looping guidance, and I found no official MiniMax guidance. The Civitai 'Fast FLF Loop Workflow — MiniMax H3' (KiwahKiwah, 2026-08-08) says that feeding the same image as first and last frame 'renders a clip that loops cleanly back to its start'. It was tested on an RTX 5080 16 GB with 64 GB RAM, using Sage + EasyCache at 15 steps: 337 s first run, 234 s warm (resolution not stated in the text). It warns EasyCache skips about half the steps and hurts detailed or character content. I found no independent reports.

NSFW-flagged community H3 finetunes on Civitai: 'H3 Eros Max' (int8 21.71 GB / bf16 40.22 GB), 'PinkCherry MiniMax H3 hybrid' (int8 21.06 / bf16 40.3 GB), 'RedCraft Hybrid H3' W6A8 22.51 GB, '10eros_Max_Int8_ref2va' 20.97 GB. They are Model Derivatives under the same license.

recommendations: Use the stack the official I2V template uses: minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot (20.97 GB) + qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq (15.69 GB, works on any NVIDIA GPU) + video_vae_int8_convrot or fp16 + audio_vae_fp32. That is about 40 GB of downloads. Avoid the full (unpruned) bf16/int8 files that Civitai used: ComfyUI's 17-frame brightness pulse would show as a visible flicker in a loop. Use pruned_bf16 only on 80 GB+ cards if you want unquantized weights.
Do not pay for NVFP4 DiT files unless the pod is Blackwell (B200, RTX 5090, RTX PRO 6000) with PyTorch cu130. On H100, L40S or A100, ComfyUI dequantizes them and int8_convrot is faster.

Pin the environment: ComfyUI 0.38–0.42 (0.38+ is needed for w6a8), PyTorch 2.12.0+cu130 (2.14.x measured about 3.7x slower on a 5090), and current comfy-kitchen. Try --disable-comfy-compiler if steps stall.
Give the pod at least 64 GB RAM for the int8 stack and 96–128 GB for bf16, or launch with --fast-disk or --disable-pinned-memory. ComfyUI's default host copy alone is about 45 GiB for the int8 stack.

Render portrait at 768x1024 for drafts and 864x1152 for finals. Both are 3:4 like your 1152x1536 art, multiples of 32, and under the 1,032,192 px cap. Prefer 124–192 frames (5–8 s) over 243: a 5 s clip costs about 0.35–0.5x a 10 s one, which matters when you need many attempts.

Start at 20 steps (official ComfyUI default); 12–16 is often enough for simple static-camera motion, so 30 is not required. For fast iteration try the lightx2v FL2VA turbo 8-step 768p LoRA at 6–8 steps with ModelSamplingMiniMaxH3 set to 6/3, or FastH3 8-step (shift 10/3). Then re-render the keeper at 20 steps with the same seed.

For loops, give the same image to first_frame and last_frame, sized exactly to the canvas (e.g. 768x1024), so the stretched first frame and center-cropped last frame are identical. Use the guide's FL2VA instruction line ('Picture 1 … aligns with the 0.00-second mark …; Picture 2 (from Shot 1) aligns with the 10.13-second mark') instead of the I2VA line your Civitai prompt used. Drop the final frame before looping so the seam frame is not shown twice.

Untested idea that could replace your crossfade trick: make a bridge clip whose first anchor is the last 5 frames of clip A and whose end anchor (MiniMaxH3AddGuide, frame_idx negative) is the first 5 frames of A. Multi-frame anchors carry motion across the seam, not just pose, so A→bridge→A could loop without a transition effect. Test it before relying on it.

Before shipping, settle the license. If you, the Runpod datacenter, or your players are in the US, EU, UK or South Korea, the community license does not cover that use or display of outputs. You would need the MiniMax application (platform.minimax.io/h3-license) or Comfy's paid license. Credit 'MiniMax H3' in the game UI and disclose AI-generated content.
unknowns: I found no ComfyUI H3 per-step benchmark on a single H100, H200, A100 or L40S; my per-GPU times are extrapolations (±40%). To settle it, rent each GPU for one session and run the official I2V template at 768x1024, 243 frames, 20 steps, fixed seed. Record s/it from the console and 'Prompt executed in'.

Whether int8_convrot's comfy-kitchen kernels are fully accelerated on Hopper (sm90) and Ampere (sm80) in ComfyUI. There are reports for sm86/89/120 and GB10, none for H100 or A100. Check the 'Native ops:' line in the load log, and compare int8_convrot vs pruned_bf16 s/it on the same pod.

Whether giving the same image as first and last frame gives a seamless loop or a stall (motion that freezes or decelerates at both ends). The only claim is one Civitai workflow description, with no independent reports. Test 5–10 seeds with a static-camera prompt; check the frame difference at the seam and look for a velocity jump.

Whether the base FL2VA weights reliably produce the explicit motion you need, or a finetune (Eros Max, PinkCherry) does better. Your Civitai success with the stock bf16 weights suggests the base works; an A/B test at a fixed seed would settle it.

Exactly which bf16 file Civitai's orchestrator loaded as '3216500.safetensors'. The primary file has no published hash, so fl2va_bf16 vs ref2va_bf16 cannot be confirmed; fl2va is implied by the use of MiniMaxH3ImageToVideo.

How the license applies to GPUs in an excluded country's datacenter, and to a game sold to US/EU players; this is a legal question. The MiniMax application form's fields and turnaround, and whether Comfy's $5,000/month license covers adult content, are unknown (the form page is JavaScript-only). Ask a lawyer and email api@minimax.io or model@minimax.io.

Whether ComfyUI's dequantized NVFP4 text-encoder path adds meaningful time on non-Blackwell GPUs. The text encoder runs once per prompt, so probably seconds, but I found no measurement. Time the CLIP encode step in the console on the pod.

found.summary:
The biggest correction: Civitai model 2821932 / version 3216500 is not a NSFW finetune. It is CivitaiOfficial's "MiniMax H3" base-model page (type Checkpoint, base "MiniMax H3"), and version 3216500 "Comfy" (published 2026-08-10) is a mirror of the Comfy-Org repack. I matched the file hashes against the Hugging Face (HF) repo: FL2VA/REF2VA DiTs at bf16 66.28 GB, int8_convrot 34.04 GB and pruned int8 20.97 GB; Qwen3-VL text encoders at bf16 51.51 / int8 27.14 / nvfp4_awq 15.69 GB; video VAE 5.21 GB; audio VAE 0.61 GB. It has no trigger words. So the user's two good clips came from plain base H3 (most likely the FL2VA bf16 primary file), with no LoRA, on Civitai's own ComfyUI workers. Downloading from Civitai needs a login or API token (verified: 307 redirect, reason=download-auth). The same files on HF Comfy-Org are ungated and free to download.

Civitai's on-site "Comfy" H3 (engine minimax-h3-comfy) costs 35 Buzz per second standard and 12 Buzz per second with turbo. That is 175 / 350 / 525 Buzz for 5 / 10 / 15 s. Resolution (up to 1344 px, multiples of 32), steps (1-60) and EasyCache do not change the price. NSFW output needs Yellow Buzz. Green and Blue Buzz are SFW-only, and civitai.com says "Unrestricted content creation has moved to civitai.red". Membership prices imply about $1 per 1,000 Buzz, so a 5 s clip is about $0.18 standard or $0.06 turbo, and the user's 10 s / 30-step clip cost about $0.35. Yellow Buzz is bought with crypto. Most of the popular NSFW LoRAs can be used on-site; the big merged checkpoints cannot.

The community ecosystem is large: 1,305 H3 resources on Civitai (879 LoRAs, 426 flagged NSFW). The most relevant ones:
- **General NSFW LoRAs:** Mystic XXX v5 (0.3 GB) and HMNSFW AIO v2.5 (0.09 GB).
- **Squeeze/jiggle LoRAs:** Boob Physics (its author says base H3 is "severely lacking in touching and squeezing physics"), Breast Play & Jiggle (best at 0.7-0.8; 1.0 can add finger artifacts) and SoftBreastMotion (0.9).
- **Checkpoints:** Eros Max (21.7 / 40.2 GB), DaSiWa (12.5-21 GB) and PinkCherry.
- **Looping:** the "Live Wallpaper" REF2VA LoRA (locked-off camera), and FLF loop workflows that feed the same image as both the first and last frame.

Repeated failure reports: turbo LoRAs give a plastic or oily look, worse audio and broken anatomy; output below about 0.7-1 MP looks noisy; faces drift; I2V can stray from the first frame (Eros Max's author suggests REF2VA instead). Nobody publishes a success rate.

People self-host mainly on Runpod (templates from Hearmeman, jalberty2018, YAW and huchukato, including a serverless worker). One report gives a PRO 6000 at about $2/hr with roughly 15 minutes of boot time.

Licensing risk: the H3 license excludes the US, EU, UK and South Korea, and also covers displaying Outputs in those places.

facts.fact: Civitai model 2821932 is 'MiniMax H3' by user CivitaiOfficial, type 'Checkpoint', baseModels ['MiniMax H3'], tag 'base model', 13,704 downloads, 1,197 thumbs-up (as of 2026-10-20). Its description calls it the open weights by MiniMax (all credit to MiniMax). It is not a community finetune.

Version 3216500 is named 'Comfy', created 2026-08-10, AIR urn:air:minimaxh3:diffusionmodel:civitai:2821932@3216500, trainedWords [] (no trigger words), and has no author notes or recommended settings. The page text says Comfy is 'the only version that takes LoRAs', with control over steps and a turbo LoRA. The other versions on the page (Api 2K, Max, HeyGen) are commercially hosted services that 'expect refusals' on content the providers decline.

Version 3216500 files, matched by SHA256 to Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3: fl2va_int8_convrot 34.04 GB (7AD4C73E6E37), ref2va_int8_convrot 34.04 GB, fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot 20.97 GB (E889202C41DA), ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot 20.97 GB, two bf16 DiTs at 66.28 GB each (primary file id 3086249; hash still 'Pending'), Qwen3-VL text encoders bf16 51.51 / int8 27.14 / nvfp4_awq 15.69 GB, video VAE fp16 5.21 GB, audio VAE fp32 0.61 GB, plus a 1.96 GB and a 0.31 GB 'Enhancement LoRA' that match no HF file (probably the turbo LoRA used on-site). All are SafeTensors.

The user's workflow path 'minimaxh3/civitai/2821932/3216500.safetensors' most likely points to the version's primary file, a 66.28 GB bf16 DiT, probably FL2VA because Civitai's imageToVideo operation uses the FL2VA weights. The text encoder came from HF Comfy-Org (qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq). No LoRA and no shift node were used.

Civitai downloads of version 3216500 need authentication: an unauthenticated request to /api/download/models/3216500 returns 307 to /login?...&reason=download-auth. The HF Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3 repo is not gated (gated: false; 25.9M downloads; created 2026-07-30, last modified 2026-09-29). Files resolve to a public CDN with no token. Recommendation: use a Runpod Pod, not serverless, for the stage where the user makes many tries and reviews them. Pick a Secure Cloud RTX PRO 6000 (96 GB, $2.49/hr on-demand, $1.69 on Community Cloud, billed per second) and a CUDA-13 ComfyUI image. Every cold worker has to reload 40-90 GB of weights, and that load counts as billed execution time. The default execution timeout is 600 s, so it has to be raised. Video output returns as base64 unless S3 is configured, and /run payloads are capped at 10 MB.

The official Runpod "ComfyUI - CUDA 13.0" template (wgd3p4n4o6, verified live) now ships ComfyUI 0.30.0. worker-comfyui can return native SaveVideo mp4s. ComfyUI's PreviewVideo.as_dict() returns {'images': [...], 'animated': (True,)}, and the handler processes the 'images' key (the 'animated' key only triggers a warning). It ignores other keys such as VHS 'gifs'.

worker-comfyui reads network-volume models via extra_model_paths.yaml (base_path /runpod-volume) with keys checkpoints, clip, clip_vision, vae, unet, loras and so on. It has no diffusion_models or text_encoders keys, but ComfyUI maps unet to diffusion_models and clip to text_encoders. So H3 files belong in /runpod-volume/models/unet, /clip and /vae.

Serverless limits: /run payload 10 MB with results kept 30 min; /runsync 20 MB with results kept 1 min. Docs say to put results that exceed these in cloud storage. Execution timeout defaults to 600 s (range 5 s to 7 days, per-request executionTimeout override). Idle timeout defaults to 5 s and is billed. Max workers default to 3. FlashBoot is on by default. Default spend limit is $80/hr. An endpoint idle for 7 days drops to max workers 0.

Serverless billing runs from worker start to stop, rounded up to the second. It includes cold start (handler ready, mostly model load), execution and idle timeout. Image pull and cached-model download are not billed. FlashBoot pauses containers with weights in VRAM and resumes in about 200 ms, but snapshots are per host and image, so bursty low-volume endpoints often miss them. A Runpod-measured 32 GB vLLM model took a 324 s median cold start from a network volume (91 s optimized).

HF model caching (--model-reference) is beta: one cached model per endpoint, and all quantizations in a repo get downloaded. Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3 totals about 525 GB, so caching it is impractical unless the user makes a trimmed copy of the repo.

Hub serverless workers for H3 exist: huchukato/runpod-minimax-h3 v1.1.3 (2026-10-20, 142 deploys) needs BLACKWELL_96, CUDA 13+, and a network volume of at least 160 GB with about 100 GB auto-download. It takes a custom job-input schema rather than raw workflows. Chsengni/runpod-minimax-h3-selflift (about 93 GB) is another. Queue a batch of seeds or prompt variants in the ComfyUI UI or the /prompt API, review the results, and queue the next batch. The models stay loaded in VRAM between runs. found.summary:
I checked the source code and ran local tests in the scratchpad. The game repo was not touched, and I opened no explicit media.

1) THE ENCODER IS THE MAIN BLOCKER. The user's ffmpeg (gyan.dev git essentials build, 2025-05-15) writes broken Theora. A 120-frame 896x1152 test file gave 118 'error in unpack_block_qpis' errors when decoded. The cause is libtheora's assembly code on Win64 builds. BtbN switched that code off on 2025-08-09 and gyan.dev did so later. A BtbN n9.0.2 build (2026-10-20) produced a clean file with 0 errors. This is probably why the user's conversion website works and local ffmpeg doesn't.

2) LOOP SEAMS. Rules that hold for any I2V model:
- Use the same still as first and last anchor, then drop the duplicate last frame.
- Make the H3 canvas the same aspect as the still (768x1024 for 3:4). The ComfyUI H3 node stretches the first frame but center-crops the last one, so a mismatched canvas gives two different anchors.
- Close the cycle with keyframes: H3's MiniMaxH3AddGuide node (ComfyUI, merged 2026-08-13) can anchor a still or a 22-frame clip at any frame.
- With post-processing only: the rotate-plus-crossfade trick, ping-pong for symmetric motion, or interpolation bridges.
I tested every ffmpeg command below for exact frame counts.

3) GODOT 4.4.1. With loop on, 4.4.1 restarts by closing and reopening the file. Seeking is not implemented and get_length() returns 0. Godot 4.5 added seeking and loops with seek(0); the Theora code has barely changed through 4.7.2. In a headless benchmark on this Ryzen AI 9 HX 370, the frame where the loop restarts took 11.2-11.7 ms on the main thread in 4.4.1 and 6.6-8.0 ms in 4.7.2. Each keyframe costs 8-11 ms and other frames about 1-3 ms. Detailed full-frame motion used about 16-17% of one core; subtle motion about 5.6%. The headless run leaves out GPU upload. .ogv files need no import step, and Theora has no alpha channel.

4) SIZES. These come from synthetic stand-in clips at 896x1152, 24 fps, GOP 64 (KiB per second of video):

| Content | q5 | q6 | q7 | q8 | q10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Detailed full-frame motion | 607 | 906 | 1273 | 1596 | 2444 |
| Subtle local motion on a static frame | 30 | 39 | 51 | 78 | 152 |

- 768x1024 is about 0.7x the size of 896x1152.
- Leaving out -pix_fmt yuv420p makes ffmpeg write yuv444p, which was 2.6x bigger.
- A larger GOP helps subtle loops a lot: g12 / g64 / g240 gave 187 / 51 / 34 KiB/s.
- 48 fps is about 1.5x the 24 fps size, and 60 fps about 1.7x.
- Upscaling 768 to 896 before encoding adds no detail. Encode at the native size and let Godot scale it.

facts.fact: VERIFIED LOCALLY: the user's ffmpeg (C:/Users/samwo/Videos/ffmpeg.exe, 'ffmpeg version 2025-05-15-git-12b853530a-essentials_build-www.gyan.dev') writes broken Theora. Encoding testsrc2 896x1152 at 24 fps with -q:v 7 -g:v 64, then decoding with ffmpeg -v error -f null, gave 118 'error in unpack_block_qpis' errors over 120 frames. The same command with BtbN 'n9.0.2-29-g6dfaba896f-20261020' (win64 gpl shared) gave 0 errors.

Root cause: libtheora's assembly optimizations break the Win64 callee-saved register convention. FFmpeg issue #20185 (2025-08-08) calls it a regression in 7.1 and master, with 7.0.2 working. BtbN disabled libtheora asm on win64 on 2025-08-09 (PR #513). gyan.dev agreed to rebuild without asm on 2025-08-21 (codexffmpeg #196). Later regressions: the 2025-09-25 gyan full build (fixed by 2025-09-28, #200) and the 2026-07-27 gyan full build (fixed 2026-07-30).

Godot docs (master, commit afce4b51f, 2026-03-21) say: 'On Windows, make sure to use 32-bit builds of FFmpeg. Windows 64-bit builds have known issues with Theora encoding, which result in artifacts.' The docs also recommend '-q:v 6 -q:a 6 -g:v 64', say -q:v 6 is a good compromise, call the default GOP of 12 too low, and say GOP 64-512 usually compresses best. They note seek times jump just past powers of two starting at 64.

FFmpeg's libtheora encoder maps -q:v (clipped to 0-10) to Theora quality q*6.3 (0-63); -b:v instead sets target_bitrate. It pads the coded frame to a multiple of 16 with pic_x = pic_y = 0. The pixel format follows the input: 420, 422 or 444.
VERIFIED LOCALLY: without -pix_fmt yuv420p, an RGB/FFV1 source encodes to yuv444p Theora. That file was 3270 KiB/s against 1273 KiB/s for yuv420p on the same content (2.6x larger).

MEASURED, synthetic stand-ins (not real H3 clips), 896x1152, 24 fps, yuv420p, -g:v 64. Detailed full-frame zoom: q5 607, q6 906, q7 1273, q8 1596, q10 2444 KiB/s. Subtle local motion over a static detailed frame: q5 30, q6 39, q7 51, q8 78, q10 152 KiB/s. At 768x1024 the same content is about 0.69-0.75x (875 vs 1273 KiB/s; 38 vs 51 KiB/s). Per-frame random grain is a worst case at 5.3-17 MiB/s. GOP effect at q7: subtle g12 187 / g64 51 / g240 34 KiB/s; heavy g12 1320 / g240 1268 KiB/s. Frame-rate effect for the same motion at q7: 24 fps 123, 48 fps 186, 60 fps 211 KiB/s.

Godot 4.4.1 source: VideoStreamPlayer with loop=true calls play() at end of stream. Theora stop() runs clear() and then set_file(file_name), which reopens the file and re-reads headers. VideoStreamPlaybackTheora::seek() only prints 'Seeking in Theora videos is not implemented yet', and get_length() returns 0. Playback time comes from OS wall-clock ticks, so time_scale is ignored.

Godot 4.5 'Theora rework' by berarma: PR #102360 (merged 2025-05-22, milestone 4.5) adds seek and get_length and loops via stop() -> seek(0), aiming at seamless loops. Other 4.5 PRs: #106825 (sync to scene tree and time_scale), #101219 (speed_scale), #106779 (UV offset when cropping), #107188 (MovieWriter can write .ogv), #107190 (libtheora 1.2.0). From 4.6 through 4.7.2 (latest stable, 2026-08-18) the Theora module only got refactors, plus an error print for files with no video stream (2026-05-26).

Godot 4.4 already contains PR #101958 (milestone 4.4, merged 2025-02-17). It fixes TH_DUPFRAME duplicate frames, frames playing ahead of time, audio and stream buffering, and cropping to picture size; before it, the main workaround was keyframe interval 1. It also has the YUV422/444 fix (cherry-picked 2025-02-14) and PR #103176 (libtheora optimizations off on x86_64 Windows GCC), which fixed frame skips and lag spikes from 4.4 RC (issue #103106).

MEASURED, headless Godot on an AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 with 896x1152 24 fps Theora (CPU decode and YUV->RGBA only, GPU upload excluded). Godot 4.4.1: the loop-restart frame took 11.2-11.7 ms on the main thread, keyframes 8.7-10.5 ms, other frames about 1-3 ms. Detailed motion used about 2.0 s CPU per 12 s (16-17% of one core); subtle motion 0.67 s per 12 s (5.6%). Godot 4.7.2 on the same files: loop restart 6.6-8.0 ms, the same as an ordinary keyframe; per-frame cost unchanged.

Code reading of both 4.4.1 and 4.5+: update() calls stop() on the first tick after the last packet, without waiting for the last frame's end time. So the last frame stays on screen only until the next process tick (about 16.7 ms at 60 Hz) instead of 41.7 ms at 24 fps. The loop comes out about one frame short.

Loop history: PR #77856 (Godot 4.1) fixed the one-frame blank or background flash when restarting on 'finished'. PR #77857 (4.2) added the VideoStreamPlayer.loop property. Docs: a non-zero 'Video Delay Compensation' setting can make loops drop frames; set it to 0.

.ogv files are not imported. ResourceFormatLoaderTheora opens the file directly as a VideoStreamTheora resource (extension 'ogv'). A video importer that would call external FFmpeg (PR #108600) is still open on the 4.x milestone. Theora has no alpha channel; the docs only offer a chroma-key canvas_item shader.

Open issue #111835 (4.5 and 4.5.1; 4.4.1 not affected): a black flash on scene change when a VideoStreamPlayer starts in _ready. Maintainers suggest putting a preview or first-frame texture underneath. Issue #92050 (open): VideoStreamPlayer draws nothing while stopped. Open PR #109209: most per-frame CPU time goes to YUV->RGBA conversion, and libyuv would be about 100% faster.

ComfyUI MiniMaxH3ImageToVideo node: first_frame is resized with crop 'disabled' (plain stretch to the canvas) and last_frame with 'center' (aspect-preserving cover crop), anchored at frame_count-1. Length snaps up to the 17k+5 grid (124 is about 5 s; the trained range is about 124-362; 243 = 10.125 s). Keyframe latents are re-injected every step and never denoised. If the still's aspect differs from the canvas, the two anchors end up as different images.

MiniMaxH3AddGuide (Comfy-Org/ComfyUI PR #15439, merged 2026-08-13) anchors a still, a clip (snapped to 5, 22 or 39... frames) and/or audio at any frame_idx; negative values count from the end, and several nodes can be chained. The PR's own examples: the first 22 frames of an existing video at frame 0 makes a continuation, and a still at frame 60 of 124 forces the clip to hit that frame. This is what a VACE-style loop bridge or a 3-keyframe I->J->I cycle would need in H3.

The official H3 prompt guide covers FL2VA (alignment line 'Picture 1 ... aligns with the 0.00-second mark ...; Picture 2 ... aligns with the S.SS-second mark') and the 'Static Shot' camera type, but says nothing about looping. Third-party guide (deAPI, 2026-08-19): pass the same image twice, end with 'every element returns to the exact arrangement of Picture 1', keep a static shot, set non_diegetic_music to N/A. It shows a 240-frame example and lists 'clip barely moves' when words describe the image rather than the action.

Civitai 'Fast FLF Loop Workflow - MiniMax H3' v1.0 (published 2026-08-08, workflow page not marked NSFW) puts the same image in first and last frame. On an RTX 5080 16GB with 64GB RAM, using SageAttention + EasyCache at 15 steps, it reports 234 s warm and 337 s cold at 1.0 MP. EasyCache skips about half the steps and hurts detailed character content.

Wan practice: the Wan 2.2 loop tutorial (Next Diffusion, 2025-09-09) puts the same image in the First-Last Frame node, runs RIFE plus Color Match, and drops the final frame 'to prevent duplication'. Wan 2.1 VACE 'Loop Anything' (nomadoor) feeds the last 15 frames, 51 gray frames and the first 15 frames so VACE fills the gap; its known flaw is washed-out first generated frames, fixed with color match. I found no primary source that measures motion stalls with identical anchors.

Kijai's WanVideoLoopArgs implements Mobius latent-shift looping: it rolls the latent along time by shift_skip (default 6) each step and un-rolls the prediction. This is training-free cyclic generation. I found no H3 equivalent.

FFmpeg docs: xfade needs both inputs at constant frame rate with the same resolution, pixel format, frame rate and timebase. Offset is measured from the start of the first input; duration is 0-60 s; the default transition 'fade' is a linear crossfade. The reverse filter buffers the whole clip in memory. minterpolate gives no output from a 2-frame input; a local test needed tpad clone padding.

VERIFIED LOCALLY (synthetic 120-frame 24 fps clips): rotate+crossfade single-clip loop gave 108 frames, first frame = A[12] and last frame matching A[11], so the seam is one natural step. Two-clip A->B->A crossfade loop gave 216 frames (LA+LB-2D). Ping-pong gave 238 (N+N-2). minterpolate bridge replacing the last 6 frames gave 120. Wrap-padded 2x interpolation of a 108-frame loop gave exactly 216 frames, with a seam step of 22.4 dB PSNR against 22.3-23.5 dB for normal steps.

Interpolation tools: ComfyUI-Frame-Interpolation (Fannovel16, updated 2026-03-29) has RIFE 4.0-4.9, FILM, AMT, IFRNet, GMFSS and others; it recommends FILM when you only have 2-3 frames. The VFI_MAMBA node in the user's earlier workflow comes from FuouM/FM_nodes and needs mamba-ssm, which has no prebuilt Windows wheel. Practical-RIFE recommends model 4.25 by default. rife-ncnn-vulkan (Vulkan, any GPU, no Python; last release 20221029, about 411 MB Windows zip) takes '-0 a.png -1 b.png -o out.png -s <0..1>'.

recommendations: FIX THE ENCODER FIRST. Replace C:/Users/samwo/Videos/ffmpeg.exe with a current BtbN win64 build or a current gyan.dev essentials build; the 2025-05-15 build writes broken Theora. A tested working copy is at C:/Users/samwo/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-samwo-OneDrive-Documents--stuff-godot2-proj-no-trace/01ada204-8b62-4981-96c5-81b32c349af3/scratchpad/dl_ffmpeg_btbn/ffmpeg-n9.0-latest-win64-gpl-shared-9.0/bin/ffmpeg.exe (temporary, in the scratchpad). Check every output with: ffmpeg -v error -i out.ogv -f null -   It must print nothing; the broken build prints 'error in unpack_block_qpis'.

THEORA SETTINGS FOR GAME LOOPS: ffmpeg -i loop_master.mkv -vf format=yuv420p -c:v libtheora -q:v 7 -g:v 240 -an loop.ogv
- Use q7 (q6 if size matters, q8 for close-ups).
- Always force yuv420p; otherwise RGB sources become 444 and come out 2.6x bigger.
- GOP 120-240 suits loops of 10 s or less: fewer 8-11 ms keyframe decodes and smaller subtle-motion files. Godot 4.4 never seeks, so a long GOP costs nothing there.
- Keep H3's native 768x1024 (3:4) and let Godot scale it (VideoStreamPlayer expand=true, or match the stills' cover/crop). Upscaling first adds no detail and costs about 30-40% more size and CPU.
- Keep width and height multiples of 16.
- Drop audio (-an). Play loop ambience from a separate AudioStreamPlayer with loop on: in 4.4 an audio track gets its resampler flushed at every restart, and H3 audio won't loop anyway.

H3 GENERATION FOR LOOPS:
- Use FL2VA with the same still in first_frame and last_frame, and write a cyclic, static-shot prompt that ends with everything returning to Picture 1, with non_diegetic_music N/A.
- Set the canvas to the still's aspect (768x1024 for 3:4 art) or pre-crop the still to the canvas. The node stretches first_frame but center-crops last_frame, so a mismatched aspect breaks the loop.
- Pick a length on the 17k+5 grid (124/141/.../243), then drop the duplicate final frame: -vf trim=end_frame=<N-1>.
- If the motion stalls near the ends, add a MiniMaxH3AddGuide mid keyframe J (an InvokeAI variant of the still, e.g. the squeezed pose) at frame_idx about N/2, so the clip runs I -> J -> I. Alternatively make two FL2VA clips I->J and J->I and join them.
- This needs your own ComfyUI on Runpod; Civitai's generator likely doesn't expose AddGuide.

BEST POST-PROCESS LOOP COMMANDS (tested; 24 fps, crossfade D = 0.5 s = 12 frames, L = clip length in seconds, N = frame count):
(a) Single clip, rotate + crossfade. The seam becomes a natural frame step and output length is L-D:
ffmpeg -i clip.mp4 -filter_complex "[0:v]settb=AVTB,fps=24,format=yuv420p,split[m][h];[h]trim=end_frame=12,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS[head];[m]trim=start_frame=12,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS[body];[body][head]xfade=transition=fade:duration=0.5:offset=<L-1.0>[v]" -map "[v]" -an -c:v ffv1 loop.mkv
(b) The user's two-clip A->B->A method, without a raw file boundary at the loop point (output length LA+LB-2D):
ffmpeg -i A.mp4 -i B.mp4 -filter_complex "[0:v]settb=AVTB,fps=24,format=yuv420p,split[a1][a2];[1:v]settb=AVTB,fps=24,format=yuv420p[b];[a1]trim=start_frame=12,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS[abody];[a2]trim=end_frame=12,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS[ahead];[abody][b]xfade=transition=fade:duration=0.5:offset=<LA-1.0>[ab];[ab][ahead]xfade=transition=fade:duration=0.5:offset=<LA+LB-1.5>[v]" -map "[v]" -an -c:v ffv1 loop.mkv
(c) Ping-pong, for symmetric motion such as a squeeze and release or breathing:
ffmpeg -i clip.mp4 -filter_complex "[0:v]format=yuv420p,split[f][r];[r]reverse,trim=start_frame=1:end_frame=<N-1>,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS[rv];[f][rv]concat=n=2:v=1:a=0[v]" -map "[v]" -an -c:v ffv1 loop.mkv
Keep crossfades short (0.3-0.6 s) and place them where motion is slow; a crossfade between two different motions shows as double exposure.

KEYFRAME-PAIR JOIN (clip1 I->J, clip2 J->I with N2 frames). Drop clip2's first frame (duplicate of J) and last frame (duplicate of I):
ffmpeg -i IJ.mp4 -i JI.mp4 -filter_complex "[0:v]settb=AVTB,fps=24,format=yuv420p[c1];[1:v]settb=AVTB,fps=24,format=yuv420p,trim=start_frame=1:end_frame=<N2-1>,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS[c2];[c1][c2]concat=n=2:v=1:a=0[v]" -map "[v]" -an -c:v ffv1 loop.mkv
If a pause or jolt shows at J or I, cut 3-6 frames on each side of the join and regenerate them with RIFE or FILM: rife-ncnn-vulkan -0 a.png -1 b.png -o t.png -s 0.25 (repeat for each timestep), or the RIFE VFI / FILM VFI nodes on the pod. ffmpeg's minterpolate (needs tpad=start=2:stop=2:start_mode=clone:stop_mode=clone around a 2-frame pair) is only a fallback; it warps hands.

H3 BRIDGE (an untested idea, but supported by the AddGuide PR): for clips that don't loop, generate a 124-frame bridge. Put AddGuide with the clip's last 22 frames at frame_idx 0 and its first 22 frames at frame_idx -22, then assemble A[22:N-22] + bridge. This is the H3 equivalent of the Wan VACE 'Loop Anything' method and keeps motion continuous across the seam. It costs one extra generation per clip.

FRAME INTERPOLATION / UPSCALING: optional.
- 24 fps on a 60 Hz screen alternates 2 and 3 refreshes per frame, which can judder on slow motion; 48 fps shrinks the steps.
- Measured cost: about 1.5x the file size and twice the decode work. A/B test 24 vs 48 in the game before committing.
- Wrap-pad any interpolation pass, or the seam loses its in-between frame. Append the first 2 frames, interpolate, then trim to exactly 2N:
ffmpeg -i loop.mkv -filter_complex "[0:v]split[a][b];[b]trim=end_frame=2,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS[h];[a][h]concat=n=2:v=1:a=0,minterpolate=fps=48:mi_mode=mci:mc_mode=aobmc:me_mode=bidir:vsbmc=1,trim=end_frame=<2N>[v]" -map "[v]" -c:v ffv1 loop48.mkv
For real use, apply the same idea with RIFE 4.25 or VFIMamba on the pod.
- Skip AI upscaling (SeedVR2, FlashVSR) unless the clips look clearly softer than the stills; it needs the same circular padding for temporal context.

GODOT 4.4.1 INTEGRATION:
- VideoStreamPlayer: loop=true, autoplay or play(), expand=true.
- Put a TextureRect with the clip's first frame (the still) underneath, so nothing flashes before the first decode or on scene changes.
- Keep Project Settings > Audio > Video Delay Compensation at 0.
- Expect an ~11 ms main-thread spike at each restart and the loop running about one frame short. Hide the seam at a low-motion moment.
- If loops still hitch, upgrading to 4.5+ (restart via seek(0), measured 6.6-8 ms) is the engine-side fix. Note 4.5's open black-flash-on-scene-change issue.
- Leave .ogv files as plain files in res://; there is no import step.
unknowns: Real H3 clip sizes in Theora: my numbers come from synthetic stand-ins. To settle: encode one real 768x1024 H3 loop at q6/q7/q8 with g64 and g240 using the fixed ffmpeg, and record KiB/s.

Does the AddGuide 22-frame bridge reproduce the anchored frames closely enough after the VAE round trip for a cut-free seam? To settle: run the bridge once and compute ffmpeg PSNR between the bridge's anchored regions and the source frames (above ~35 dB should be invisible).

Will the measured ~11 ms Godot 4.4.1 restart spike plus the shortened last frame be visible on the user's display with vsync and normal game load? The benchmark was headless and left out GPU upload. To settle: play a loop in the actual game with the Godot profiler and a frame-time graph, at 24 fps and 48 fps.

Mobius-style latent-shift looping for H3: there's a Wan implementation (WanVideoLoopArgs), but none for H3. H3's nested video+audio latent and 17k+5 temporal grid may not tolerate a circular roll. Would need a custom node test.
Whether gyan.dev's current builds (2026-10-19) are clean: BtbN n9.0.2 tested clean; gyan has regressed twice before. To settle: run the decode-check command on any new build before trusting it.

Node order is BackgroundImage, FullscreenAnim, VideoStreamPlayer, Fade, so the clip draws over its still and under the black fade.

The still is a TextureRect of 897x1193 with expand_mode 4 (EXPAND_FIT_HEIGHT) and stretch_mode 4 (STRETCH_KEEP_ASPECT, anchored top-left). The user is mostly right. As of 20 Oct 2026, MiniMax H3 is where open-weights NSFW video work is happening, and the best evidence is creator activity on Civitai. Its public API lists 872 H3 LoRAs, all first published since Aug 2026 (213 in Aug, 384 in Sep, 275 in Oct 1-20). Over the same months, new Wan 2.2 I2V LoRAs fell to 7, 10 and 3, LTX-2.3 to 38, 13 and 0, and LTX-2.5 got only 43 in total. Several big Wan NSFW LoRAs are adding H3 versions.

The H3 LoRAs already include ones that fit this project exactly: "Breast Play & Jiggle for MiniMax H3" (its v2 is first-last-frame), "Live Wallpaper Style" (an H3 Ref2VA version for subtle, seamless loops, Sep 23) and "H3 Eros Max". The vendor tests I found also favour H3. Floyo (Aug 2026, one generation per model on an H100) ranked it first for motion and temporal consistency.

"The only real way" overstates it, though. Wan 2.2 I2V-A14B is Apache 2.0 and its NSFW ecosystem is mature: "WAN 2.2 Enhanced NSFW" has 410k downloads and DR34ML4Y has 515k. It has first-last-frame support built into ComfyUI and is much faster: 26.7 s for a 720p I2V clip on a 5090 using LightX2V's own 4-step NVFP4 build, against 2685 s at 40 steps. Its weaknesses are a native 16 fps / 81 frames (about 5 s) and less natural motion than H3. The DR34ML4Y author, who has trained the same LoRA on H3, Wan and LTX, still calls Wan 2.2 I2V their best NSFW I2V; their H3 version is only a preview from Oct 17.

The other models don't suit this job:
- **LTX-2.5:** about 3x faster than H3 (28.7 s vs 81.2 s for about 5 s on a 5090), but it has few NSFW LoRAs and its Gemma text encoder handles NSFW poorly.
- **HunyuanVideo 1.5:** 8.3B parameters, no first-last-frame mode, and its NSFW community has gone quiet.
- **Kandinsky 6.0:** MIT licence, weights out Sep 2026, but first-frame I2V only and no community around it yet.
- **Wan 2.5, 2.6, 2.7 and 3.0, and FLUX 3 Video:** API-only or not released.

Two findings matter more than the model choice:

**Licence.** H3's licence excludes the US, EU, UK and South Korea. It forbids using or distributing the model "or any of their Outputs" outside the allowed territory, and it requires commercial products to display "MiniMax H3" prominently. Wan 2.2 (Apache 2.0) has neither problem.

**Looping.** H3's first-last-frame mode is built for loops: put the same image in as both the first and last frame. A community workflow does exactly that. However, node-pack authors report that these clips "almost always end in a locked, barely-moving tail", so the frozen end has to be cut off before the loop point.

It leads on motion quality, it is where the NSFW community is building (LoRAs, merges, loop workflows), it runs at 24 fps natively and has a first-last-frame mode. 'The only way' is wrong, though: Wan 2.2 I2V-A14B is a mature, Apache-2.0, much faster fallback that runs in the same ComfyUI.

Before using H3 clips in a game you distribute, check the licence. It does not cover the US, EU, UK or South Korea, Section V.4 also restricts its outputs there, and commercial products must show 'MiniMax H3' in their interface. If the user or their storefront or players are in those regions, Wan 2.2 (Apache 2.0) is the clean choice. HunyuanVideo 1.5 excludes the EU/UK/Korea but not the US. For loops, replace the ping-pong splice with H3's first-last-frame mode using the same still as both first and last frame (Civitai 'Fast FLF Loop Workflow', 2843813). Then measure and cut the frozen tail (FL2VA lands on the last frame and holds it), and crossfade about 4-8 frames at the seam to hide VAE colour drift. Alternative: render A→B and B→A as two first-last-frame clips so motion never reverses.

Try the LoRAs built for this shot type: 'Live Wallpaper Style' (H3 Ref2VA version, also Wan 2.2) and 'Breast Play & Jiggle for MiniMax H3' (v2.0 is first-last-frame). Use turbo LoRAs only for drafts, since the DR34ML4Y author reports they weaken NSFW concepts. Do finals at about 20-30 full steps.

gaps_researched.question: Does Runpod's ToS actually forbid private adult/NSFW video generation on pods, and is it enforced? (This decides whether Runpod is viable at all.)
gaps_researched.answer:
The literal text bans it; enforcement against private use is not evidenced. Verified: the ToS (Last Updated March 24, 2026), Section 6, lists 'pornography or graphic adult content, images, or other adult products' among unauthorized Content and says 'Postings of any unauthorized products or content may result in immediate termination of your account and a lifetime ban'. Section 7 adds 'Your Content is not obscene, lewd, lascivious ... (as determined by us)'. There is no separate AUP and no 'NSFW' clause.

Context that cuts the other way:
- The ban is framed around Content 'submitted to', 'posted' on or 'made available' through the Service.
- Section 2 says 'the Service does not include your applications or Your Content'.
- Section 7 says Runpod 'will not actively monitor Content'.
- Section 7 also asks customers to keep 'age-restricted content on our Site' from minors and to stop minors seeing 'harmful or inappropriate material on your site', which assumes such content exists.
- Runpod's own blog (published 2024-12-03, updated 2026-09-13) spotlights AnonAI, a customer with 'No limits, safeguards, or restrictions in place', and adds '(note: potential adult themes may be displayed, proceed with discretion.)'.
- Runpod's Hub lists 'MiniMax H3 Uncensored' templates and workers (per the runpod researcher).
- Runpod's security docs say hosts may not inspect pod data.

I found no report of an account ban for private NSFW generation; Reddit was not reachable, and third-party analyses (cling-ai, now 410) also found no explicit rule.

Conclusion (medium confidence): there is a real but unquantified contractual risk, and no evidence of enforcement for private, unpublished generation. To reduce it, never expose outputs on the public port-8188 proxy URL or share links from the pod, pull files down over SSH, and don't publish anything from Runpod. If the user wants certainty, they can ask support for a written answer.
sources: Runpod MCP search-docs (site namespace, ToS sections 6-7), 2026-10-20
